#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
engine="$PWD/strata-inkling"
control="$PWD/control"
weights="$PWD/weights"
pack="$weights/Inkling-2-Mini-SQ-10.strata"
test -x "$engine"
printf '%s  %s\n' ac4d452ad03e4930abd9d46f9c5eec22b2f75a1da45a1e49bd24ccd58b065934 "$pack" | sha256sum -c
if [[ ! -x "$control/bin/strata" ]]; then
    archive=strata-control-0.1.65-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
    curl -fsSL "https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/releases/download/v0.2.19/$archive" -o "$archive"
    printf '%s  %s\n' b44caf1980731edf2a0cdf9170cffdd8d240da87663016b6cb04f612582300d3 "$archive" | sha256sum -c
    mkdir -p "$control"
    tar -xzf "$archive" -C "$control"
fi
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$PWD${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"
printf '%s  %s\n' 7f332727f9a3f093dd452a39cc978e6757627e5dad1b0673aa4e75174f236dd6 "$weights/tokenizer.json" | sha256sum -c
"$control/python/bin/python3" "$control/tools/inkling_tokenizer.py" --hf-json "$weights/tokenizer.json" \
    --template "$weights/chat_template.jinja" --out "$PWD/tokenizer"
"$control/python/bin/python3" - "$engine" "$pack" "$control" <<'PY'
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path
engine, pack, control = sys.argv[1:]
root = Path.cwd()
profile = {
    "exe": engine, "args": ["--native", pack, "--max-context", "131072",
                            "--vram-experts-gb", "8.60", "--ram-experts-gb", "0.00", "--kv", "k8v4"],
    "cwd": control, "tokenizer": str(root / "tokenizer"), "model_name": "inkling-2-mini-sq-10",
    "arch": "inkling2_loop", "log": str(root / "strata-inkling.log"), "lib_dirs": [str(root)],
    "port": 18735, "drafting": "dspark", "parallel": 1, "gpu": 0,
    "gpus_asked": True, "open_browser": False,
}
profile["args_written"] = profile["args"].copy()
(root / "inkling-profile.json").write_text(json.dumps(profile, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
exec "$control/bin/strata" serve --offline --profile "$PWD/inkling-profile.json" --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18735

setup: One RTX 3060 12 GB. K8V4 uses about 1.54 GiB of mapped host KV in addition to other process allocations. The tested system had 32 GiB of RAM. Peak total board use was 11,758 MiB in long-context qualification.
